display.purpose: Section titles: Projects, Experience, Technologies, About.

name.purpose: The developer name on the lintel; smaller than the verse.

numeral-passage.purpose: The 01 left standing in the dark behind the doors.

numeral-book.purpose: Volume number at the foot of each cover.

verse.purpose: Gate verse on paper slips, horizontal, sized from both axes.

headline.purpose: Open project title in the detail panel.

period.purpose: Dates left of the cord, tabular figures.

poem.purpose: Verse on a book cover, Mincho, max 16ch.

strip.purpose: Technology name on its paper strip, Mincho.

label.purpose: Field labels, status, placeholder notes. Never an eyebrow above a heading.

seal-initials.purpose: Initials in the hanko seal, SVG units.

shadows.name: door-edge
shadows.purpose: Inner door edge as the doors part; mirrored on the right door.

shadows.name: paper-age
shadows.purpose: Inner glow on the paper doors.

shadows.name: hanging-tag
shadows.purpose: The resume tag; technology strips use 0 10px 16px -8px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.7).

shadows.name: seam-glow
shadows.purpose: Light leaking at the gate seam.

shadows.name: cover-glow
shadows.purpose: Faint violet light under book covers on void.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Bar slide-in (0.4s), book rise and dim (0.5s), tassel drop (0.45s), tag sway (0.5s), verse ink-in (0.8s), panel-in (0.5s).

motion.name: weighted-wood
motion.purpose: Door parting; slow to start, decisive at the end.

motion.name: open-ms
motion.purpose: Timed opening played by the cord, a downward scroll, or a menu link; the gate is scroll-locked until then.

motion.name: passage-timeline
motion.value: pull 0-0.12, door 0.03-0.55 (weighted), flood 0.10-0.58, black 0.55-0.70, head 0.80-0.90 of a 170svh track
motion.purpose: Gate passage phases, including the held black beat.

motion.name: scroll-driven
motion.value: animation-timeline: view() on the thread cord, knots, strips (swing), About scroll (unroll) and close doors (shut)
motion.purpose: Section arrivals; all gated on prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: flap
motion.value: scaleX 1 to 0.35; companion 0.34s, perched 1.6s; gate butterflies 1.6s and 1.25s
motion.purpose: Butterfly wings; reduced-motion disables the gate loop.

motion.name: snap
motion.purpose: Ghost-to-struck colour changes on nav and links.

textures.name: grain-paper
textures.purpose: Paper fibre on doors, covers, strips, slips, scroll, close buttons.

textures.name: grain-wood
textures.purpose: Wood grain on lattice bars, planks, rollers, door pulls.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Senkaimon Verse"**

The site is a passage through a gate and then a room of paper and wood behind it. Black lacquer frames every region, cool washi paper carries the words, dark grained wood holds what is shelved or rolled, and the space beyond the gate is a velvet black lit only by taking darkness away. One vermilion cord runs through the whole system: it is the control at the gate, it becomes the line that experience and technologies hang from, and its colour marks every action a visitor can take. Everything else is held in ghosted greys until it is struck.

Density is low and deliberate. Type is large, sections are tall, and the content holds one thing at a time: on the gate the doors and their verse; on the shelf one pulled-forward book; on the scroll one unrolled sheet. The gate is locked shut until the visitor pulls the cord, pushes down, or follows a menu link, and then a timed opening plays. Motion is heavy and decisive, like weighted wood; ghost-to-struck states snap with no transition. Bleach is evoked through original material (gate, paper, lacquer, cord, hanko seal, ink butterflies), never through borrowed artwork.

All copy and project data in the shipped build is placeholder by design and is marked as such in the interface; nothing here describes real projects, employers, or biography.
keyCharacteristics: Four materials: lacquer frames, washi paper, grained wood, void depth.
One accent, vermilion, for the cord, controls, and the red ink of the seal and stamps.
Three type voices: heavy display gothic, Mincho for anything written or spoken on paper, quiet gothic for UI and prose.
Square surfaces and structural borders; the only rounding is on turned wood (door pulls, scroll rollers) and the focus ring.
Tactile texture from two tiling SVG grains (paper fibre, wood grain), never from image files or photography.
Light and focus conveyed by removing darkness, not by adding colour.

rules.name: The One Cord Rule
rules.body: Vermilion marks the cord and what hangs from it, what can be acted on (controls, links, focus), and the owner's red ink (the hanko seal and the stamped facts). It never decorates headings, fills sections, or tints imagery.

rules.name: The Removal of Darkness Rule
rules.body: Focus and arrival are shown by lifting a shade (unchosen books sit dimmed to 55% brightness and rise to full when chosen; the passage floods with seam light), not by adding colour or brightness to the focused thing.

rules.name: The Cool Paper Rule
rules.body: Paper is washi (cool, slightly green-grey). The paper-shade browns only age its edges; never warm the paper itself toward cream or parchment.

rules.name: The Spoken Line Rule
rules.body: Mincho is for lines written or voiced on paper (verse slips, cover poems, the About lead, organisation names, technology strips). It never sets UI, labels or buttons.

rules.name: The Numbered Registry Rule
rules.body: Destinations and volumes carry two-digit display numerals (01, 02...). Numbers are part of the name, set in the display face.

rules.name: The Label Is Data Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked labels name a field, a status, a group or a destination. They never sit above a heading as an eyebrow.

rules.name: The Planes Not Cards Rule
rules.body: Elevation comes from one material sitting in front of another (lacquer over paper, paper over void, books on planks). Do not add generic card shadows to lift content off a background.

rules.name: The Two Grains Rule
rules.body: Paper surfaces take the paper-fibre grain and wooden parts take the wood grain, nothing else is textured. Grain is a tiling SVG token, never an image file, and never laid over text-bearing vermilion or the void.

dos: Do frame every region in lacquer, put words meant to be read slowly on washi paper, and shelve or roll things on grained wood.
Do keep vermilion to the cord, controls, links, focus, and the owner's red ink (seal, stamps); use Lit Vermilion on black and Deep Vermilion on paper.
Do show state by snapping ghost to struck, with no colour transition on hover.
Do show focus or arrival by lifting darkness (dimmed books, seam flood) rather than adding colour, and add a non-colour cue (underline) wherever colour marks the chosen item.
Do number destinations and volumes with two-digit display numerals.
Do apply the paper grain to paper and the wood grain to wood, through the `--grain-paper` and `--grain-wood` tokens.
Do use a fluid clamp() from the documented ramp for any new type size, and add a ramp step here when a genuinely new one is needed.
Do honour reduced motion: the gate stays whole, the page is unlocked, and nothing parts, swings, draws, or unrolls.
Do keep every interactive target at least 44px tall and every placeholder visibly labelled.
donts: Don't warm the paper toward cream or parchment.
Don't introduce a second accent colour or use vermilion on headings or section backgrounds.
Don't round surfaces or controls; corners stay square apart from the 2px focus ring, door pulls, and scroll rollers.
Don't set UI, buttons or labels in Mincho.
Don't place uppercase tracked labels above headings as eyebrows.
Don't use official Bleach artwork, logos, characters or quoted text; gate, cord, seal and butterflies are original drawings.
Don't use image files or photography for texture; grain is the SVG tokens.
Don't use bouncy or elastic easing for state changes; motion is weighted and decisive.
